key_insight: For the supervised classification tasks studied, boosting noisy quantum classifiers meets the same accuracy target with fewer circuit executions than probabilistic error cancellation, avoiding ideal-output reconstruction.
engineering_relevance: Task-aware ensembles could reduce quantum sampling costs by exploiting labeled data and useful information retained in noisy circuit outputs.
method: Compare boosted noisy parameterized quantum circuits with probabilistic error cancellation at a shared learning target.
Establish a common classification-risk upper bound when empirical margin loss matches, for specified architectures under Pauli noise.
Evaluate AdaBoostR and Real AdaBoost in finite-shot teacher–student simulations.
evidence_signal: Across simulated circuit depths and physical noise strengths, boosting required fewer circuit executions as depth and noise increased and achieved higher test accuracy than the corresponding reference.
watch_item: The advantage is task-dependent and demonstrated in simulations with specified architectures and Pauli noise; broader hardware validation remains necessary.
paper_title: Beyond Error Mitigation: Using Boosting for Noisy Quantum Machine Learning
